method.design: Randomized blocks; one run per variant and Go reference in each block; unmodified server ACK behavior; no memory sampler.
method.metric: Sum of response-sent to next primary-request-received across five dependent tool steps, in milliseconds.
method.bootstrap: 5000 paired-block resamples, percentile95% interval; descriptive uncertainty on this machine, no population guarantee.
method.predeclared_target: Both changes: median and nearest-rank p95 tool-gap time below Go reference for each measured transport.

model.critical_path: T_tool = sum_i(C_i + A_i + R_i + S_i), for the five causally ordered model/tool rounds; C=useful processing, A=avoidable ACK wait, R=exit-detection delay, S=other scheduling/IO waits.
model.dependency_bound: For arbitrary parallel work, completion time >= longest dependency-path cost. These benchmark tool rounds form a chain, so concurrency cannot legally reorder them.
model.tcp_wait: A_i ~= I_i * max(0, D_ack - elapsed_i), D_ack approximately40ms observed here. Nagle can hold the next small write pending an ACK; the server needs that write to produce its reply. TCP_NODELAY removes this added gate without changing TCP byte ordering.
model.poll_wait: For exit at delay d>0 after the first unsuccessful wait4 and repeated polling every P: R(d)=P*ceil(d/P)-d. Here P=100ms. If phase moduloP were uniform, E[R]=P/2 and p95=.95P, conditional on entering polling. Short-lived shell EOF/exit races can instead place d near0, producing almostP delay. The experiment does not assume uniform phase.
model.pidfd: pidfd_open plus poll waits for the actual kernel exit event. Exit-detection delay becomes wake/scheduler latency rather than timer quantization; a100ms maximum poll timeout still bounds cancellation checks. On unsupported/restricted kernels the old bounded polling fallback is retained.
model.factorial_effects: Let mu00,mu10,mu01,mu11 be mean latencies with TCP_NODELAY and pidfd off/off,on/off,off/on,on/on. Average TCP saving=(mu00-mu10+mu01-mu11)/2; average pidfd saving=(mu00-mu01+mu10-mu11)/2. Their sum equals mu00-mu11. Interaction=mu11-mu10-mu01+mu00.
model.interpretation: Averages and bootstrap intervals describe these paired randomized blocks on this machine. They do not prove universal latency bounds or transfer the result to different model/network workloads.

validation.server_ack_policy: unchanged default for every ablation run
validation.variant_changes: only net.o and tools.o differ among native variants
